html:
Brunei is a small Malay Muslim sultanate on the north coast of Borneo. The map shows it from 1650 to 2010, but its history goes back much further. Chinese records speak of envoys from a kingdom called Boni in the 900s, and its rulers turned Muslim in the 1300s; tradition dates the first sultan to 1368, though the date is debated.

Brunei's high point came around 1500 under Sultan Bolkiah, when it claimed most of the coasts of Borneo and had influence as far as Manila. Survivors of Magellan's voyage visited in 1521, and Antonio Pigafetta described its rich court. Spain attacked and briefly held the capital in the Castilian War of 1578. It was one of the Malay Islamic sultanates of the age.

Then came a long decline:

  • the Sultanate of Sulu took its northeastern lands;
  • in 1841 it granted Sarawak to James Brooke, whose family kept taking more;
  • the British North Borneo Company took the north from 1881;
  • Brunei became a British protectorate in 1888, and in 1890 Sarawak seized Limbang, which split Brunei into two pieces.

Oil found at Seria in 1929, and pumped with Shell, made the tiny state rich. Brunei chose not to join Malaysia in 1963 and became fully independent in 1984 under Hassanal Bolkiah, sultan since 1967, who rules as an absolute monarch.
